name: Graceful Degradation & Brownouts
tagline: Protecting core user journeys (auth, checkout, payments) during traffic spikes or dependency outages by shedding P2/P3 features in prioritized tiers.
purpose: Build a progressive mental model of graceful degradation—from P0–P3 criticality tiering and adaptive load shedding to circuit breakers, bulkheads, and hysteresis.

spark.summary: Graceful degradation protects core user journeys during traffic spikes or dependency outages by shedding non-essential features (recommendations, live counts, heavy analytics) in prioritized tiers before core paths fail.
spark.keyTakeaway: When a single bottleneck threatens end-to-end availability, classifying endpoints and features into P0–P3 criticality tiers—paired with adaptive load shedding, circuit breakers, and stale-cache fallbacks—keeps checkout and auth at 99.99% availability even at 5x normal load.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** Without deliberate degradation tiers, a brownout in a non-critical dependency (personalized ML recommendations, `'12 people viewing'` counters, or review stars) exhausts caller thread pools and DB connections—dragging down login and checkout in a cascading 503 blackout.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Priority Load-Shedding & Hysteresis State Machine (NORMAL (All Tiers) -> BROWNOUT (Shed P3) -> CRITICAL (P0/P1 Only)); Priority Gateway -> P0 Core Path vs. Shed P2/P3 Fallback (Envoy Priority Shed -> P0 Checkout / Auth -> P2 ML Recs Bulkhead -> Redis Stale Fallback).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Combine local concurrency limits with edge cache fallbacks for defense in depth. At the API gateway (Envoy/Nginx), priority-aware load shedding drops P3/P2 traffic first, while inside each service, per-dependency bulkheads and circuit breakers degrade optional calls to cached defaults.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Dive into concrete production problems on priority load shedding, bulkheads, circuit breakers, and retry storms.

learningJourney.title: What is Graceful Degradation

explanation.foundation: Without deliberate degradation tiers, a brownout in a non-critical dependency (personalized ML recommendations, `'12 people viewing'` counters, or review stars) exhausts caller thread pools and DB connections—dragging down login and checkout in a cascading 503 blackout.
explanation.core: **Graceful degradation** classifies every RPC and feature into **criticality tiers (P0–P3)**: **P0** (auth, payment capture, order placement), **P1** (cart, search), **P2** (ML personalization), and **P3** (reviews, view counters). Under overload, gateways and services shed P3 then P2 first so P0 stays at 99.99% availability.
explanation.deepDive: In production deployments of Graceful Degradation & Brownouts, watch how what is graceful degradation interacts with tail latency, retry amplification, and partial failures. Graceful degradation protects core user journeys during traffic spikes or dependency outages by shedding non-essential features (recommendations, live counts, heavy analytics) in prioritized tiers before core paths fail.

ideas.description: P0 security, auth, and inventory-lock checks must **fail closed** (reject on timeout); P2/P3 enrichments **fail open** to empty lists or stale-if-error caches.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Graceful Degradation & Brownouts without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: When a single bottleneck threatens end-to-end availability, classifying endpoints and features into P0–P3 criticality tiers—paired with adaptive load shedding, circuit breakers, and stale-cache fallbacks—keeps checkout and auth at 99.99% availability even at 5x normal load.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

decisionExercise.prompt: When Graceful Degradation & Brownouts experiences a sudden 5x traffic spike alongside a slow downstream dependency, which engineering choice best protects system stability?

options.label: Increase retry counts and remove client timeouts so every request eventually succeeds.
options.explanation: Unbounded retries multiply load on an already struggling dependency and exhaust worker pools.

options.label: Enforce strict latency budgets, bounded jittered retries, and graceful fallback or load shedding.
options.explanation: Bounding retries and isolating slow paths preserves healthy capacity and keeps tail latency predictable.

learningJourney.title: Where Degradation Belongs (and Where Failing Closed is Mandatory)

explanation.foundation: Think of **Where Degradation Belongs (and Where Failing Closed is Mandatory)** as the intuition layer for Graceful Degradation & Brownouts: Scope boundary: identify where this pattern fits best and where simpler or async alternatives win.
explanation.core: Apply graceful degradation at user-facing gateways and optional enrichment fan-outs; never fail open on financial or security invariants.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, where degradation belongs (and where failing closed is mandatory) becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Graceful degradation protects core user journeys during traffic spikes or dependency outages by shedding non-essential features (recommendations, live counts, heavy analytics) in prioritized tiers before core paths fail.

benefits: Sheds ML reranking, view counts, and review widgets to keep cart/checkout fast at 6x load.
costs: Fallback paths must be exercised in regular game-day drills so they don't crash during real incidents.

comparison.choice: Good Candidate: LLM Copilot Model Fallback
benefits: Trips circuit breaker on primary reasoning model 429s and routes P1 summarization to a faster fallback model.
costs: Slightly lower answer richness during upstream provider rate-limit storms.

comparison.choice: Avoid Fail-Open: Auth, Fraud & Ledger Writes
benefits: Failing closed protects financial integrity and security boundaries.
costs: Failing open on auth or rate-limiting creates immediate security vulnerabilities.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why should an automated brownout/load-shedding controller use hysteresis (e.g., shed P3 when CPU > 80% for 10s, restore only when CPU < 60% for 60s)?

options.text: To prevent rapid oscillation (flapping) between normal and degraded states when load hovers near the threshold
options.feedback: Correct: hysteresis and cooldown windows stabilize the system and prevent flapping.

options.text: To allow P3 requests to bypass authentication during recovery
options.feedback: Hysteresis only stabilizes state transitions; auth is P0 and never bypassed.

options.text: To disable circuit breakers permanently after an incident
options.feedback: Hysteresis enables safe automatic recovery once load drops well below the trigger.
